title: Ruy Lopez: Closed
line: The main line: White builds a big center slowly, and both sides maneuver.

steps.text: The Ruy Lopez: the bishop attacks the knight, and Black asks it to decide.
The bishop steps back, both sides bring a piece out, and White castles.
Put your rook behind the pawn on e4. It guards the pawn, so now your bishop really threatens to take the knight and then the pawn on e5.
Black's pawns chase the bishop. Step it back: on b3 it still aims at the pawn on f7.
Move the pawn on c2 one square. It gives the bishop a way back and gets ready for a pawn on d4.
Push the pawn on h2 one square, so no black piece can jump to g4 and pin or hit your knight.

also.a2a4: Attacking the pawns on the queen side is also played. This lesson stops the pin first.
also.d2d4: Pushing to the center at once is also played. This lesson stops the pin first.

steps.text: Step the bishop back to c2. From there it aims along the other diagonal, toward h7 by the black king.
Now push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. With the pawn on c3 behind it, you have a big center.
Bring the knight out, behind your pawns. It can go on toward f1 and g3 later.

also.d4d5: Closing the center with the pawn is also played. This lesson keeps the center as it is.

steps.after: This is the Closed Ruy Lopez: a slow fight, with plans on both sides of the board.

summary: Rook behind the center pawn, bishop kept on the long diagonal, the pins stopped, and then a big pawn center.
